newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's Etete blasts Shell over LNG project.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's Etete blasts Shell over LNG project.

text.p: Oil minister Dan Etete, who sacked the board of directors of the Nigerian LNG Limited (NLNG) last month, on Thursday accused Shell Gas BV, the technical leader in the joint venture, of frustrating the project.

"Shell, instead of using its position as an independent technical adviser to the advantage of the project, has used this position to subject other shareholders to its whims and caprices," Etete told the shareholders whom he summoned to a meeting in his office in the capital Abuja.
"Shell has consistently frustrated all efforts to officially carry out the foundation laying ceremony of the project by the head of state," he added.
There was no immediate response from Shell.

NLNG insists that the $4 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) project, black Africa's biggest project, is on course and last month NLNG new chief executive, Steve Ollereanshaw, said it was slightly ahead of schedule and was 40 percent complete.
But two weeks later Etete unceremoniously sacked the board of directors of the company, saying this was to lay "to rest some unhealthy developments threatening the company's accountability."
The four shareholders in the project are state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp, Shell Gas BV, Elf Aquitaine and Agip SpA.
They are financing it from their own funds and have placed $2.873 billion in escrow accounts to execute the project.

Etete said several measures that should have been put in place to involve Nigerians and other shareholders in the project had not been done and he set out a timetable for each of the issues on which he said Nigeria was aggrieved to be redressed.

"The shareholders agreement must definitely be reviewed urgently. Until these are resolved, the management of NLNG would continue to report to the honourable minister as the government representative on the project," he said.

The Nigerian LNG project, which has set 1999 as the date when gas will be delivered, has suffered several postponements in the past and frequent management changes but the present military government has generally shown more commitment to it.
Etete said the government had made many concessions to Shell in recognition of the company's expertise in the gas business.
"Instead these very concessions have been used to marginalise government's interest in the project," he said.
The project is to produce 7.5 billion cubic metres of gas annually for delivery to customers in Spain, France and Turkey.
The fourth and biggest buyer, Enel of Italy, terminated the contract in December and the issue was now before an arbitration panel in Switzerland.
Etete reaffirmed Nigeria's commitment to the project.

"Likewise, I would like other shareholders to formally confirm and pledge in writing and submit to my office their continued commitment to the execution of this very important project within the next 48 hours," he said.
